_readme: Independent monthly cost benchmarks for a retiree household, used by
scripts/verify-affordability.ts to calibrate the model.
This is the ONLY check that can catch a constant that is sourced but wrong.
Plausibility bounds and coverage reports verify internal consistency; only
real observed costs verify that the model is pointed at reality.
The current entries use the UMass Boston 2025 Elder Index for one adult
age 65+, in good health, who owns a home without a mortgage. The Index
includes housing, health care, food, transportation, and miscellaneous
essentials at county-level market costs. It is an independent model, not
a sample of this app's inputs, so it can expose systematic calibration bias.
Aim for 8-10 cities spread across the price range - a couple cheap, a
couple expensive, several mid. Clustering them all in one band hides
systematic bias.
Fill `entries` with objects shaped like:
"city": "Pueblo, Colorado",
"tenure": "own_outright",
"actualMonthlyCost": 2850,
"source": "how you arrived at this - listings, a local budget, ACS",
`id` must match locations_location.id. `tenure` is one of own_outright,
buying, or rent. The harness fails above 20% error on any entry.
